long-haul = travelling a very long distance by air, often between continents
layover = a wait at an airport between two parts of a journey
turbulence = sudden rough movement of a plane caused by air currents
rush hour = the busy time of day when many people travel to or from work
connecting flight = a second flight that you take after changing planes
charter flight = a flight hired for a tour group, not a regular scheduled service
low-cost airline = an airline that sells cheap tickets and charges extra for many services
boarding gate = the door and waiting area where you enter the plane
cabin baggage = bags you take into the cabin rather than putting in the hold
excess baggage = luggage heavier or larger than the airline's free limit, charged extra
baggage allowance = the weight or number of bags you may take without extra fees
overhead locker = the compartment above the seats for cabin bags
frequent-flyer programme = a scheme that gives points or upgrades to regular passengers
upgrade = a move to a more comfortable class of seat, sometimes free
economy class = the cheapest, most basic seats on a plane
business class = a more expensive cabin with extra space and service
red-eye flight = an overnight flight that arrives early in the morning
missed connection = failing to catch the next plane, train or bus in time
airbridge = a movable corridor that connects the terminal to the aircraft door
in-flight service = food, drink and help offered by cabin crew during a flight
